text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent midweek newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An officer of the Directorate on Corruption and Economic Crime is in England to investigate the whereabouts of a former Air Botswana general manager, wanted in Botswana on allegations of corrupt practice.

- Members of the Evangelical Luthern Church in Botswana (ELCB) on Sunday used bolt cutters to break their way past wire fences to enter the Lutheran Church in Gaborone, barricaded against them by members of the Lutheran Church of Southern Africa (ELCSA).

ELCB is a breakaway faction of the church seeking full autonomy in church matters and was formed 18 years ago, when ELCSA obtained a Court order to bar ELCB members from the churches, but did not try to enforce it until recently.
- Air Botswana is seeking government approval to increaase its passenger fares by three percent because of a recent 27 percent rise in the price of aviation fuel.
